description: Hi, I am Ayushman Sahoo and I am a tech enthusiastic in the field of AI and ML and I am open to learn new things.
summary: Proving Grounds helps mission teams choose where on Earth to rehearse for the Moon and Mars. It ranks 25 km patches of Earth by how closely their terrain matches three NASA targets: the Shackleton Connecting Ridge on the Moon (rover mobility), Arcadia Planitia and Deuteronilus Mensae on Mars (ice access). Each target and each Earth patch is described by slope distribution, roughness and relief from NASA LOLA and MOLA elevation data, compared at a matched scale and scored with task-specific weights. This addresses the challenge by finding and characterizing new candidate analogs with open data, and by testing the method against known analogs such as Atacama and Death Valley. It matters because analog sites are usually picked by reputation. Every result comes with an uncertainty range, a note on where Earth fails, and a field-validation plan, so the output is a shortlist for field checking, not a claim of proof.
details:
What it does and how it works

  • A Python pipeline downloads the Moon target, clips the Mars targets from the USGS MOLA model, and loads Copernicus elevation tiles for 8 known analog regions and 14 candidate regions.
  • A bare-ground mask drops vegetated windows. Earth is averaged to the target’s pixel scale, and each 25 km window is scored on three similarities: slope distribution (Earth Mover’s distance), roughness ratio and relief ratio.
  • An interactive map lets users switch targets, move weight sliders that re-rank everything live, and open a site profile showing the match, where Earth fails, and a downloadable field-validation plan. The top 10 can be downloaded as CSV.

Benefits and intended impact

  • Moves analog selection from reputation to measurement, matched to the task (driving vs. ice access).
  • Shows how stable each rank is: each candidate gets a rank range when weights vary by 20%.
  • Intended impact: give teams a ranked, transparent shortlist of sites to check in the field, and a method others can extend with new data layers.

Results so far (Moon target)

  • 187 windows in 17 regions were scored. Known analogs rank at a median of 7th of 17 regions, against about 9th expected by chance. This shows mild consistency, not proof.
  • 7 of the 8 known analogs had usable data; Haughton Crater was dropped.
  • The best Earth match for the ridge scores only about 51% (Altiplano-Puna), so no Earth site is a close twin. [Add the Mars results once you’ve reviewed them.]

Tools

  • Python 3.13, NumPy, SciPy, rasterio; Leaflet with HTML/JavaScript for the viewer; hosted on Vercel; run on a Windows laptop.

Creativity

  • Matching by task rather than a single similarity map.
  • A backtest that compares known analogs against chance, after I dropped a biased metric.
  • Rank uncertainty, “where Earth fails” notes and a field plan on every site.

Factors considered

  • Matched resolution across Moon, Mars and Earth data.
  • Land cover (vegetation hides terrain).
  • Weights are assumptions, not fitted to the known sites.
  • Terrain only: no thermal, mineral or illumination layers yet. Earth cannot match vacuum, low gravity, radiation or cold.
